name: MonarchEventChip
title: EventChip
wrapsNative: Button with a custom ButtonStyle; Text, Circle, RoundedRectangle
summary: One event in a calendar view: a colour dot or bar, the title, the time and the status, as a button that opens the event or as a label.
whenToUse: For each event in a month cell (dot), an agenda or all-day row (bar) or a time grid (block).
whenNotToUse: Not for a status without a time (use MonarchBadge) and not for a selectable filter chip. For a whole calendar that belongs to the device, EventKitUI shows the person's own events.
api: init(_ title: String, time: String? = nil, timeLabel: String? = nil, detail: String? = nil, color: Color? = nil, status: MonarchEventChipStatus = .confirmed, variant: MonarchEventChipVariant = .dot, isPast: Bool = false, statusLabel: String? = nil, isCompact: Bool = false, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchEventChipStatus: String { case confirmed, tentative, cancelled, declined }
enum MonarchEventChipVariant { case dot, bar, block }

options.name: time
options.description: The visible time, already formatted. Leave it out for an all-day event in an all-day row.

options.name: timeLabel
options.description: The time as VoiceOver reads it when time is abbreviated, such as "9:30 to 10:15" or "All day".

options.name: detail
options.description: A second, muted line in bar and block chips.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's colour, for the dot, the bar and the tint only. nil is the theme's accent.

options.name: isPast
options.description: The event has ended: muted title and a faded marker.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the status, in the visible word and in the spoken name.

options.name: isCompact
options.description: A block chip on one line, time then title, without the status word and the detail.

options.name: action
options.description: Opens the event. With it the chip is a Button; without it a label.

states.name: confirmed
states.description: A filled dot or a solid bar; bar and block chips have a light tint of the event colour.

states.name: tentative
states.description: A hollow dot or a dashed bar, a lighter tint and a border in the event colour. The status word is drawn in bar and block chips and spoken in all.

states.name: cancelled, declined
states.description: Muted text, the title struck through, the marker in the strong border colour and a muted fill instead of the tint. The status word is drawn in bar and block chips and spoken in all.

states.name: past
states.description: Muted title and the marker at reduced opacity.

states.name: pressed
states.description: With an action: a dot chip gets the muted fill, a tinted chip a stronger tint, a cancelled chip the emphasis fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) stops the action. The look does not change.

appearance: Text uses the default and muted text colours of the theme in every theme. The event colour (the accent unless the app gives one) is the dot, the bar and a tint laid over the surface colour at 14 percent. The app's colour is used as given in light, dark and high contrast, so choose one that is visible on both canvases.
platformNotes: The same statuses, variants and compact density as the web and Android. The web chip is always a button or a link; here the action is optional, and a link is an action that opens the URL. The web's asChild is not needed: wrap the chip in a NavigationLink instead. The web tints with color-mix; here the event colour is drawn over the surface at the same ratio. Hover is the pressed state.
accessibility: One element read as "title, time, status, detail". The status is left out when confirmed and the detail in a dot chip.
timeLabel replaces the visible time in the spoken name.
With an action the element has the button trait and a touch target at least 44 points high; the visible chip stays compact inside it.
The status is never colour alone: a hollow or dashed marker, a struck-through title, and the status word.
The text scales with Dynamic Type. A dot chip is one line and wraps at the accessibility sizes.
edgeCases: A block chip fills the frame it is given and clips what does not fit. A frame under 44 points high with an action overlaps its neighbours' touch targets.
A long title in a dot chip is truncated at the standard sizes.
In a bar chip the time moves under the title when both do not fit on one line.
isPast is not spoken; the time already says when the event was.
An empty title leaves the spoken name to the time and status.

examples.title: Dot chips (month cell)
examples.template:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
    MonarchEventChip({{events.0.title}}, time: {{events.0.time}}, color: hex(0x{{events.0.color|raw}}), status: {{events.0.status|case}})
    MonarchEventChip({{events.1.title}}, time: {{events.1.time}}, color: hex(0x{{events.1.color|raw}}), status: {{events.1.status|case}})
    MonarchEventChip({{events.2.title}}, time: {{events.2.time}}, color: hex(0x{{events.2.color|raw}}), status: {{events.2.status|case}})
    MonarchEventChip({{events.3.title}}, time: {{events.3.time}}, status: {{events.3.status|case}})
}
.frame(width: 220)
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
    MonarchEventChip("Stand-up", time: "09:00", color: hex(0x0f766e), status: .confirmed)
    MonarchEventChip("Design review", time: "11:00", color: hex(0x7c3aed), status: .tentative)
    MonarchEventChip("Retrospective", time: "16:00", color: hex(0xc2410c), status: .cancelled)
    MonarchEventChip("Vendor call", time: "17:30", status: .declined)
}
.frame(width: 220)
